note: Take Root API is egress-blocked from this container (curl to api.takeroot.bible returns 000). The Kulish text was fetched instead from the ebible mirror on raw.githubusercontent.com (gracious-tech/fetch_collection, bibles/ukr_pan), all 66 books, and every span below was lifted from it byte-for-byte rather than typed.
Jer 49:11a — «Полиши тілько твої сироти, я не дам їм загинути» — one of the two texts he held on to in prison.

REVIEWER: Jeremiah 15:11 is a TEXTUAL DIVERGENCE, not a translation choice. Bunyan quotes the AV's 'Verily it shall be well with thy remnant'; Kulish reads «Конець твій буде добрий» — 'your end shall be good'. Same consolation, different sentence. Kulish is quoted verbatim, as the skill requires, but the English's wording is not recoverable from it. This is the Qere/Ketiv-class hazard the skill flags for Job and the Prophets, and it is an editorial call, not a defect to patch.
Job 1:9b — «Чи то ж Йов дармо такий богобоязливий?» — Satan's question, the word that ended his despair. Recorded as 'b': the verse opens with the narrative frame he does not quote.
'Thy righteousness is in heaven' is NOT scripture and is not recorded as such — Bunyan reports it as a sentence that fell on his soul, and it is rendered as his words.
The Esau passage (Heb 12:16-17) is alluded to, never quoted, so nothing is claimed for it.
